title: Frontiers in neuroimmunology
objective: Name open questions in neuroimmunology and connect them to the lab's work.

steps.title: Where the field is going
steps.body: Open questions abound: which sensory subtypes carry which neuroimmune jobs, how spinal/[[DRG]] afferents (not just vagal) participate, how the circuits differ by organ, and whether tuning them could treat inflammatory disease. The spinal/DRG side, and organs beyond the gut, are wide open.

steps.prompt: Why is the spinal/DRG side of neuroimmune control a frontier?
options: Most of the classic reflex work is vagal; the DRG side is far less mapped
The DRG has been clearly shown to have no immune-related role of any kind
It was fully solved long before the vagal reflex work had even begun
Spinal sensory neurons are simply unable to release any neuropeptides at all
steps.explanation: The inflammatory reflex is a vagal story; which DRG subtypes do analogous jobs, and in which organs, is largely unmapped — exactly the lab's kind of question.

variants.prompt: Why is the DRG side still open?
options: It's far less mapped than the vagal side is
It has no immune-related role at all in the body
It was already solved first, before the vagal work
variants.reveal: The DRG side of neuroimmune control is largely uncharted.

steps.setup: Your project silences pancreas-innervating sensory neurons and reads out physiology.
steps.prompt: How does it fit neuroimmunology's frontier?
options: It probes the understudied DRG side in an organ beyond the gut
It merely repeats the vagal inflammatory-reflex work already done
It abandons neuroimmune questions and research entirely
It only re-describes the colon findings that already exist
steps.reveal: Taking subtype-specific DRG tools to the pancreas extends neuroimmune and interoceptive mapping to a new organ on the understudied spinal side — the through-line of this whole app.

variants.prompt: The pancreas DREADD project sits at the neuroimmune frontier because it…
options: Probes the understudied DRG side in an organ beyond the gut
Merely repeats the existing vagal reflex work already done
Drops the neuroimmune questions from the project entirely
variants.explanation: It extends DRG-side tools to a new organ.

sources.citation: Wallrapp A & Chiu IM, 2024, Annu Rev Immunol

reviewNotes: Neuroimmune frontiers; DRG side; pancreas project. Caps Track B.
